purpose: lists the services, toolchains, tools, and settings kit runs with

--text.description: prints the stages as text, even on a terminal

--json.description: the stages as one JSON object: stages, then each stage's document under its name, null for one that could not be read

--jq.description: the same JSON, formatted by jq for a person

--stages.description: prints the stages, one per line, in order, the same over any workspace

--marks.description: prints a mark per stage, as one JSON object, which changes when what the stage draws does: a hash of kit.yml for settings; for toolchains and tools, of the files the toolchains and the dependency providers pin from and of those that keep kit's choice; and for services, of all of those, the clone's git configuration, which holds its remotes, and .kit/policy

services.description: {capability, service, provider, chosen, ready}: capability is hosting, review, ci, releases, tracking <prefix>, toolchain, dependencies <provider>, or policy, and dependencies alone where no provider's manifest and lock are here; service is what answers it, as github, mise, or patterns, null for none, as for the forge's with no remote or a ci the forge lacks; provider is kit's module that reaches it, as forge/github; chosen is set where kit.yml or a recorded choice names it, else inferred; ready is whether its tool is there and signed in, null where it has none. A forge or a policy engine kit.yml names wrong is {error}, its line, under errors

toolchains.description: {provider, role, usable, active, chosen, fills}, as kit toolchains --json prints them, keyed by provider and role: mise project

tools.description: {name, pinned, installed, from}, as kit tools --json prints them, keyed by from and name; ambient, {name, path, from}

settings.description: {setting, value, from}: value is kit.yml's, or the schema's default, null where it names none; from is set or default
